claim_type_rationale: The universe rule is deterministic and source-defined by closed canonical NBER designation: NBER Business Cycle Dating Committee maintains the official US business-cycle table with peak/trough dates, and Wikipedia's `List of recessions in the United States` master article enumerates the 'Great Depression onward' section with 15 NBER-dated recessions (peak month ≥ August 1929). The benchmark window scope clause ('peak month >= August 1929') is documented per audit cycle-2 confirmation. Universe membership = 'NBER-dated US recession with peak month ≥ August 1929 per NBER official table + Wikipedia master Great Depression-onward section' — no curator judgment. Per-row cell values (Peak Year + Trough Year + Duration Months from NBER official table; Recession name + Peak Unemployment Rate from Wikipedia master) are source-extractive. Peak Unemployment Rate uses the locked extraction rule: 'strip % and parenthetical month/year; if master gives a range, use the highest endpoint' (handles Great Depression cleanly as 24.9 from master cell '21.3% (1932) – 24.9% (1933)'). Mirror precedents for closed-canonical-list source_defined with explicit benchmark window: `phanerozoic_periods_by_start_age` (12-period Phanerozoic closed ICS universe with explicit eon-scope); `decade_volcanoes_by_continent` (16-entry IAVCEI closed list).

collection_summary.approach: Pre-curation design pass (2 rounds of pre-staging design review: cycle-1 + cycle-2). Cycle-1 verdict: 'Revise Before Cycle-0 Staging' with 2 BLOCKING design issues — (a) source_count=1 was wrong because Wikipedia master doesn't have a clean Cause/Primary Trigger column (it has Characteristics narratives) and NBER is the upstream authority for peak/trough/duration; (b) Primary Trigger categorical cell was too curator-judgment-heavy with multi-causal narratives. After cycle-1 audit's two options (A = drop Primary Trigger / cleaner; B = keep Primary Trigger / candidate_rebuild + row-by-row rationale), **Option A taken** because (1) audit-corrected trigger labels would make Monetary tightening dominate 8 of 15 rows = weakly-discriminating causal cell, and (2) clean source-extractive temporal schema aligns better with the gap-1 chipping goal. Cycle-2 verdict: 'Approve for Cycle-0 Staging, With 3 Required Staging Edits' — all applied at cycle-0: (1) Recession of 1937–1938 peak unemployment 20.0 → 17.8 per master; (2) recession names locked to master-table row labels with en-dash year-range formatting; (3) Peak Unemployment Rate normalization rule documents range-extraction handling. 2-round pre-staging review matches the mirror-precedent `decade_volcanoes_by_continent` pattern (2 design rounds + 2 post-staging cycles).
collection_summary.partition_structure: Closed canonical 15-recession NBER-dated US universe with explicit benchmark window scope (peak month ≥ August 1929). Per-era partition (informational, not staged): Great Depression era 2 (Great Depression + 1937-1938); WWII/Korean War demobilization era 3 (1945 + 1949 + 1953); Bretton Woods era 4 (1958 + 1960-1961 + 1969-1970 + 1973-1975); Volcker era 2 (1980 + 1981-1982); Post-Volcker financial-era 3 (1990-1991 + 2001 + 2007-2009); Pandemic era 1 (COVID-19 2020). Single PK Recession.
collection_summary.row_count_check: 15 rows match the closed 15-recession NBER-dated benchmark-window universe (peak month ≥ August 1929). NBER's full chronology extends back to 1854 but is explicitly out of scope per the benchmark-window scope clause documented in table_title + normalization_decisions.

validation_cross_checks.rationale: Per artifact-contract.md: validation sources do not count toward source_count and live in source_coverage_notes prose rather than registered source_urls. The 14 distinct per-recession Wikipedia URLs below (covering 15 row mappings — `1980 recession` and `1981–1982 recession` both map to the shared `Early_1980s_recession` article) were consulted during curation as validation sources for each recession's NBER dates and unemployment values. They are documented here for provenance transparency. None of these validation sources carries a universe role for the staged set; the universe role is carried by the NBER official table + master. Per-recession articles may carry redundant value role for some cells (same Peak Year/Duration appears in both the master table and per-recession infoboxes) but are kept as validation cross-checks per the periodic_table_groups + decade_volcanoes + phanerozoic_periods precedents.

decision_log.rationale: NBER Business Cycle Dating Committee maintains the official US recession-dating chronology back to 1854. The 1929-present benchmark window is a deliberate scope choice (aligns with Wikipedia master's 'Great Depression onward' section break + provides iconic Great Depression anchor + 15 rows comfortably above the 10-row gate). Per cycle-2 audit: 'claim_type=source_defined is acceptable with the explicit benchmark window NBER-dated contractions with peak >= August 1929.' Distinct from candidate_rebuild (no curator-bounded universe selection) and partially_supplemented (no rebuilding of the master subset).

decision_log.decision: Primary Trigger column dropped (Option A from cycle-1 audit)
decision_log.rationale: Cycle-1 audit flagged Primary Trigger as too curator-judgment-heavy: (a) the master's Characteristics column has multi-causal narratives (e.g., 1990-1991 = 'Fed rate hikes, oil shock, debt accumulation, consumer pessimism' — not cleanly Financial crisis); (b) audit-corrected labels would make Monetary tightening dominate 8 of 15 rows = weakly-discriminating causal cell. Cycle-1 offered two options: A = drop Primary Trigger / cleaner source_extractive schema with no causal secondary; B = keep Primary Trigger / candidate_rebuild + row-by-row rationale. **Option A chosen** because (1) the causal cell would be poorly discriminating after corrections; (2) clean source-extractive temporal schema better aligns with the gap-1 chipping goal; (3) the user's request for 'strong causal' angle becomes harder to defend after seeing the actual master content. Trade-off: instance loses the causal secondary axis; preserved only as primary = temporal.

decision_log.decision: Universe source = NBER official table + Wikipedia master (source_count = 2)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit BLOCKING fix: 'Wikipedia master table has Name / Period Range / Duration / ... / Characteristics, not a clean Cause or Primary Trigger column. NBER is the official source for peak/trough months and contraction duration... Use source_count=2: NBER official business-cycle table for peak/trough/duration, plus Wikipedia List of recessions in the United States for row names and characteristics/trigger narratives.' Cycle-2 audit confirmation: 'source_count=2 is the right source plan: NBER official table for peak month, trough month, and contraction duration; Wikipedia master for row labels and peak unemployment.'

decision_log.decision: Benchmark window = 1929-present (peak month ≥ August 1929); NBER full chronology back to 1854 out of scope
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit: 'The 1929-present cutoff is defensible: it aligns with the Wikipedia section break Great Depression onward, gives 15 rows, includes the iconic anchor recession, and avoids the noisier pre-1929 chronology. NBER's monthly chronology itself runs back to 1854, so the cutoff must be explicitly described as a benchmark window, not the full NBER universe.' Benchmark window explicitly described in table_title + normalization_decisions::Recession.rule + this decision_log entry.

decision_log.decision: Recession names = master-table row labels (NOT per-recession article canonical titles)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit note + cycle-2 audit's required staging edit #2: 'Use master-table recession labels consistently. If the rule is name per master-table row label, stage these labels, not mixed article-title/common-title variants.' Audit specifically flagged 6 labels requiring en-dash + master-form correction: Recession of 1937–1938, Recession of 1945, Recession of 1949, Recession of 1953, 1973–1975 recession, 1981–1982 recession (replacing the cycle-1 preview's 'Early 1980s recession' which is article-style not master-row-label). For consistency, en-dash applied to all year-range names including Recession of 1960–1961 and Recession of 1969–1970. Non-year-range names preserved: Great Depression / Recession of 1958 / 1980 recession / Early 1990s recession / Early 2000s recession / Great Recession / COVID-19 recession.

This handles the Great Depression cleanly as 24.9 (master cell expresses '21.3% (1932) – 24.9% (1933)' — highest endpoint = 24.9). Locked extraction rule documented in normalization_decisions.

normalization_decisions.rule: Recession name verbatim per Wikipedia master `List of recessions in the United States` row label (NOT per-recession article canonical title — some rows share Wikipedia articles like Early 1980s recession covering both 1980 and 1981–1982 entries). 15 closed values: Great Depression / Recession of 1937–1938 / Recession of 1945 / Recession of 1949 / Recession of 1953 / Recession of 1958 / Recession of 1960–1961 / Recession of 1969–1970 / 1973–1975 recession / 1980 recession / 1981–1982 recession / Early 1990s recession / Early 2000s recession / Great Recession / COVID-19 recession. Year-range pairs use en-dash (–) NOT hyphen (-) per master table convention; cycle-2 audit specifically flagged 'Early 1980s recession' as article-style (NOT master row label) and required '1981–1982 recession' instead.

Integer year of NBER-dated peak month per NBER official business-cycle table. Examples: Great Depression peak August 1929 → 1929; COVID-19 recession peak February 2020 → 2020; 1948-1949 recession peak November 1948 → 1948. For recessions where Peak Year = Trough Year (1945, 1980, 2001, 2020), staged identical values. Benchmark window scope: Peak Year ≥ 1929 (peak month ≥ August 1929 per NBER table).

Integer year of NBER-dated trough month per NBER official business-cycle table. Examples: Great Depression trough March 1933 → 1933; COVID-19 recession trough April 2020 → 2020; 1948-1949 recession trough October 1949 → 1949. May equal Peak Year for short within-calendar-year recessions (1945, 1980, 2001, 2020).

Integer months of NBER-published peak-to-trough contraction duration per NBER official business-cycle table. Examples: Great Depression 43 months (Aug 1929 → Mar 1933); COVID-19 recession 2 months (Feb 2020 → Apr 2020 — shortest NBER-dated recession on record); 1981-1982 recession 16 months (Jul 1981 → Nov 1982 — Volcker disinflation era second-longest).

Numeric percentage extracted from Wikipedia master table's Characteristics column per the cycle-2 audit-locked extraction rule: 'Use the numeric peak unemployment percentage from the Wikipedia master table; strip % and parenthetical month/year; if the master gives a range, use the highest endpoint.' Examples: Great Depression master cell '21.3% (1932) – 24.9% (1933)' → highest endpoint 24.9; Recession of 1937–1938 master cell '17.8%' → 17.8 (NOT 20.0 — cycle-2 audit's required staging edit #1 corrected the cycle-1 preview's best-guess value); 1981–1982 recession master cell '10.8% (December 1982)' → strip parenthetical → 10.8; COVID-19 recession master cell '14.7% (April 2020)' → 14.7. Pre-1948 BLS unemployment data uses historical Lebergott / Romer estimates (different methodology than post-1948 BLS series); Wikipedia master's stated values preserved per Tier B Wikipedia convention.

open_questions.question: When NBER declares the next US recession after 2020 COVID, should this instance be re-staged to include it?
open_questions.answer: Yes, when NBER's Business Cycle Dating Committee officially declares the next contraction with peak month and trough month, this instance can be extended to 16 rows. No active recession as of 2026-05-18 staging. Universe is locked to NBER-dated recessions as of staging date; future NBER declarations would warrant a follow-up cycle. temporal_sensitivity = low reflects that NBER declarations are formal and infrequent.

open_questions.question: Should the benchmark window cutoff be 1929 (current — 15 rows), 1854 (full NBER — 34 rows), or post-WWII 1945 (13 rows)?
open_questions.answer: Locked to 1929-present per cycle-1 audit's defensibility note: 'aligns with the Wikipedia section break Great Depression onward, gives 15 rows, includes the iconic anchor recession, and avoids the noisier pre-1929 chronology.' Other cutoffs are valid alternative scopes but the 1929 cutoff combines (a) clean Wikipedia section alignment, (b) ≥10-row gate satisfaction, (c) iconic Great Depression anchor, (d) modern unemployment data availability (pre-1929 unemployment estimates are noisier).

open_questions.question: Why drop Primary Trigger (causal secondary) — wasn't the original motivation 'strong causal angle'?
open_questions.answer: Cycle-1 audit found (a) Wikipedia master's Characteristics column has multi-causal narratives that don't cleanly map to a categorical Primary Trigger; (b) audit-corrected labels would make Monetary tightening dominate 8 of 15 rows = weakly-discriminating causal cell. The 'strongest causal-flavored temporal candidate' framing turned out optimistic — the actual master content doesn't support clean cause attribution. Option A taken: drop Primary Trigger / clean source_extractive schema. The causal-evaluation angle can be picked up by a future instance where the cause-effect column is genuinely discriminating (e.g., per-pathogen disease outbreaks where each row has a distinct pathogen-cause). Trade-off documented; preserved temporal benchmark value.

open_questions.question: Should pre-1948 unemployment values (Great Depression, 1937-1938 recession, 1945 recession) use BLS-published values or Wikipedia master values?
open_questions.answer: Wikipedia master values per the staged Tier B Wikipedia convention. Pre-1948 unemployment data uses historical Lebergott / Romer estimates (different methodology than post-1948 BLS Current Population Survey series). The master table reflects historical estimates with explicit citation; staged values preserve master's stated values. Audit confirmed master's values are extractable for all 15 rows per the locked extraction rule.

open_questions.question: Should the schema include Peak Month / Trough Month for finer time precision?
open_questions.answer: No — Peak Year + Trough Year + Duration (Months) together convey the temporal information with sufficient precision (Duration in months captures sub-year detail). Adding Peak Month + Trough Month would add 2 cells with limited additional benchmark value while increasing schema complexity. Cycle-1 audit offered Peak Month / Trough Month / Peak Unemployment as the 3 Option A alternative cells; Peak Unemployment was chosen as the most informative 5th cell.
